paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about Daniel. He reads the word of the LORD to Jeremiah, sees that the desolation of Jerusalem would last seventy years (Daniel 9:2), and he doesn't just sit back and say "well, it's on the calendar." He gets down in sackcloth and ashes and PRAYS (Daniel 9:3). God's promise is never a reason to stop talking to God.

Now look at HOW he prays. He starts with who God is, "the great and awesome God, who keeps His covenant of loving devotion" (Daniel 9:4). He says "we have sinned" and counts himself in, and he says they are not coming "because of our righteous acts, but because of Your great compassion" (Daniel 9:18). I open most of my prayers with "Hey, so, quick favor," and Daniel is over here teaching me class.

And then, friend, God answers before Daniel even finishes. Gabriel says, "At the beginning of your petitions, an answer went out" (Daniel 9:23), and he calls Daniel "highly precious." The answer reaches far past seventy years, to an end to sin, atonement for iniquity and everlasting righteousness (Daniel 9:24), with the Messiah, the Prince, named along the way (Daniel 9:25). It's a heavy message, but it tells us God's plan is bigger than our prayers, and that He hears the humble ones, so keep praying, baker, and keep the ovens ready.
